title: THE SUN FROM EARTH
narration: This is the Sun as we know it. Half a degree wide, and eight minutes away at the speed of light.
Now stand on Mercury. The Sun is more than twice as wide, and almost seven times brighter.
From Venus it would look a little bigger than ours, if you could ever see it through the clouds.
Before we go further, look up from Phobos. Mars fills almost half of the sky.
From Mars the Sun has already shrunk to two thirds of the size we are used to.
At Jupiter it is a small, hard disc. Sunlight here is twenty seven times weaker.
From Saturn the light has been travelling for well over an hour.
At Uranus the Sun is barely a disc at all.
And from Neptune it is the brightest star in a black sky, four hours of light away.
